Helium is a text language model backbone built from scratch to provide strong reasoning abilities to the system [P1][P3]. Mimi is a neural audio codec that uses residual vector quantization and distills semantic knowledge to convert audio into discrete tokens [P1][P3][P4]. Moshi is the overarching multi-stream speech-to-speech Transformer model that enables full-duplex spoken dialogue [P3]. The architecture combines Helium with a smaller Transformer to predict audio tokens in a hierarchical and streaming fashion [P4]. Moshi jointly models the audio streams from both the user and the system, along with Moshi’s text tokens, using a Depth Transformer [P3]. This multi-stream design allows the model to speak and listen simultaneously without explicitly modeling speaker turns [P3].

H-Net employs a hierarchical architecture comprising three primary components: encoder networks (E), a main network (M), and decoder networks (D) [P1]. In a single-stage model, the architecture consists of one encoder network, one main network, and one decoder network [P1]. The encoder networks must simultaneously preserve fine-grained information for transmission to their corresponding decoders via residual connections and compress inputs into chunks of richer representations for the main network [P2]. The main network operates on these progressively compressed sequences, allowing for larger networks within the same computational budget [P3]. The decoder networks effectively combine the coarse-grained representations from the main network with the fine-grained details from the encoder residuals [P2]. Both the encoder and decoder networks operate on uncompressed sequences, which makes computational efficiency a significant design constraint [P2].
